title: Install ayamai on the game consoles
body: PS5 and Xbox have no user shell and no browser worth using; Switch has neither. Realistic: a console browser pointing at the LAN door for the media surfaces, not the platform. Record what each console's browser actually supports before promising anything.

title: Device install matrix: mac minis, laptops, Linux boxes, phones
body: One checklist per class of machine, each with the evidence that it works: node source (tarball vs brew vs distro), hosts entry, port 80 mechanism (launchd / systemd / netsh portproxy), autostart, doctor output. The Mac laptop is done; a second Mac and a fresh Linux box are next.

title: Add a per-project activity signal endpoint that returns last-touched timestamp and open-work count
body:
from idea #1 · A way to see which projects are quiet and which are on fire, at a glance

Expose a single read endpoint on the platform that, for each registered project, returns the most recent activity timestamp and the count of open items (uncommitted files, open plans, pending intake). Done when the endpoint returns data for all six projects and a contract test pins the response shape.

title: Define quiet and on-fire thresholds as configurable platform settings
body:
from idea #1 · A way to see which projects are quiet and which are on fire, at a glance

Add named settings for the quiet cutoff (no activity for N days) and the on-fire cutoff (open items above M or activity within H hours), with sane defaults and a documented precedence order. Done when the thresholds can be changed without a code deploy and the signal endpoint reflects the new values.

title: The platform can say what is stale
body:
One endpoint, one panel row: for each project, last commit, last plan event, last publish, open item count, and health. The panel currently shows what is running; it never shows what is neglected.

Absorbs the retired #18 (activity signal), #19 (quiet/on-fire thresholds) and #6 (activity covers more than imports), plus seiri's since-last-visit idea.

Acceptance: gehirn shows, for every registered project, a last-touched timestamp and an open count, and a contract test pins the endpoint's shape.

title: Install ayamai on the other machines
body:
A mac mini, this laptop, and the TV in the living room. One item, a checklist per host — not three items. Absorbs the retired #17 (install matrix), #15 (TV) and #16 (consoles as far as a controller-free box allows).

The point is not coverage, it is proving the install story on a second OS and a second class of machine.

Acceptance: 'ayamai doctor' passes on at least one non-WSL host, and the door answers from that host's browser.

title: yoru survives its own machine
body:
Verify the library reads with the network unplugged, then take the second copy of the vault. Absorbs the retired #3 and #2.

The product works; this is about it still working after a disk dies, which is the half of local-first that has to be earned rather than claimed.

Acceptance: a restore from the second copy is performed once, on a scratch directory, and written down.

title: Decide the fork: Chromium, Electron, or the web
body:
yoru's browser story has been an item for a month. It is a decision, not a task: one page of tradeoffs, a recommendation, and then it is closed either way. Absorbs the retired #10.

Acceptance: a one-page decision note in docs/, a recommendation, and this item closed — whichever way it goes.

title: Azahar's first patch
body:
The 3DS fork exists, is pinned at 2127.0-alpha4, and carries no diff of its own. A fork with no patches is a bookmark. The first patch is what makes it ours — build it on Windows, then change one thing that matters for our library.

Acceptance: the fork builds, one patch is committed to ayamaiio/azahar, and gemu's child row reads ours with a non-zero patch count.

title: Spotify import seeds taste on day one
body:
Spotify's API never gives audio, but /me/top/tracks and /me/player/recently-played give taste. Importing them on connect means uta is useful before you have played anything locally.

Acceptance: connecting Spotify fills artist affinity from top tracks, and the next song starts from it

Raised by 53cbaa4

title: Add a reference by name, not by URL
body:
Pasting a link is the fallback. Searching YouTube's Data API by title and saving the result is what you actually do when a song is in your head.

Acceptance: typing a title returns matches and one keystroke saves the chosen one as a reference

Raised by 53cbaa4

title: One queue across owned files and references
body:
Today the queue is owned-only and references open in their service. Interleaving them is what makes it one library: play a file, then hand off to Spotify for the next track.

Acceptance: the next button can return either kind, and a reference plays through its service without leaving the page

Raised by 53cbaa4

title: Radio: seed the next song from one track
body:
A stationary scorer discovers slowly. Seeding from a chosen track — same artist, same era, co-occurring in your playlists — is how you get from one song to an evening.

Acceptance: a track can be used as a seed and the following ten picks stay in its neighbourhood

Raised by 53cbaa4

title: Decide on ZealOS: fork it, vendor a build, or leave TempleOS alone
body:
TempleOS runs under QEMU as a guest (gemu/templeos). ZealOS is the fork that is still maintained, and Shrine is a separate C++ interpretation. Forking ZealOS means taking on the HolyC toolchain and its maintenance; vendoring a built image means tracking someone else's releases; leaving it alone costs nothing and keeps the machine read-only. The three are different commitments and only one of them is a project.

Acceptance: a decision recorded in the gemu/templeos README, and if a fork: a child project with its upstream commit and a patch of our own

title: yoru finds the machine's media and imports it on one press
body:
uta now walks every drive through packages/core/scan.mjs. yoru needs the same walk with the media extension set (image/video), but its import is different in kind: it copies bytes into the library and creates posts. So: POST /api/library/discover writes a report (counts by folder, sample paths) and touches nothing; the Library page shows 'found N files across M folders - import'; one press runs the import through the extracted local-import core (signature check, content-addressed object write, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), with progress and cancel. scripts/import-local-dir.mjs becomes a thin wrapper over the same module.

Acceptance: with an empty library, yoru reports what exists on the machine; nothing is written until a press; a second import is a no-op; cancel leaves committed batches and no half-written objects
